title: Security Council resolution 635 (1989): Marking of plastic or sheet explosives for the purpose of detection
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 635, adopted on 14 June 1989, on marking plastic or sheet explosives so that they can be detected. In it the Council condemns all acts of unlawful interference against the security of civil aviation and calls on all States to cooperate in measures to prevent terrorism, including acts involving explosives. It is the source for milestone T028 and links aviation security to the detection of explosives.

title: Security Council resolution 731 (1992): Libyan Arab Jamahiriya (Pan Am 103 and UTA 772)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 731, adopted on 21 January 1992, concerning Libya and the investigations into the destruction of Pan Am flight 103 and UTA flight 772. The Council condemns the destruction of the two aircraft and the loss of hundreds of lives and states it is determined to eliminate international terrorism. It is the source for milestone T031 and was followed by sanctions in resolution 748 (T032).

title: Security Council resolution 748 (1992): Libyan Arab Jamahiriya sanctions
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 748, adopted on 31 March 1992, imposing measures on Libya. It decides that the Libyan Government must comply without further delay with the requests made under resolution 731 regarding the Pan Am 103 and UTA 772 investigations, and must commit definitively to cease all forms of terrorist action and assistance to terrorist groups. It is the source for milestone T032.

title: Security Council resolution 1189 (1998): Bombings in Nairobi and Dar-es-Salaam
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1189, adopted on 13 August 1998, after the bombings in Nairobi and Dar-es-Salaam. The Council strongly condemns the bomb attacks of 7 August 1998 in Kenya and Tanzania, which it says claimed hundreds of lives and injured thousands, and calls on States to support the investigations in Kenya, Tanzania and the United States. It is the source for milestone T043.

title: Security Council resolution 1267 (1999): Afghanistan (Taliban sanctions; 1267 Committee)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1267, adopted on 15 October 1999, concerning the Taliban in Afghanistan. It decided that all States would impose measures from 14 November 1999, including denying landing and take-off rights to aircraft owned, leased or operated by or for the Taliban, and it established a Security Council committee (the 1267 Committee) to oversee them. Later CTA6 milestones record that the regime was extended and renamed and then adapted to include ISIL (T104, T116), and that its listings were challenged in court (the people-disagree milestone T097).

title: Security Council resolution 1269 (1999): Responsibility of the Security Council in the maintenance of international peace and security (terrorism)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1269, adopted on 19 October 1999, on the Council's responsibility for international peace and security in relation to terrorism. It calls on all States to fully implement the anti-terrorism conventions they are party to, to consider joining the others, and to cooperate through bilateral and multilateral arrangements. It is the source for milestone T047 and is one of the Council's general resolutions on terrorism before September 2001.

title: Security Council resolution 1368 (2001): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1368, adopted on 12 September 2001, the day after the 11 September attacks. The Council states it is determined to combat by all means threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts, and in its preamble recognizes the inherent right of individual or collective self-defence under the Charter. It is the source for milestone T051.

title: Security Council resolution 1373 (2001): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (Counter-Terrorism Committee)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1373, adopted on 28 September 2001. It decides that all States shall prevent and suppress the financing of terrorist acts, criminalize the provision or collection of funds for them, and refrain from supporting entities or persons involved in terrorist acts, and it calls for faster exchange of operational information. It also established the Counter-Terrorism Committee (milestone T055); later resolutions such as 1535 and 2462 build on it.

title: Security Council resolution 1438 (2002): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (Bali)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1438, adopted on 14 October 2002 after the bomb attacks in Bali, Indonesia, on 12 October 2002. The Council condemns the attacks 'in the strongest terms', regards them, like any act of international terrorism, as a threat to international peace and security, and expresses condolences to Indonesia and the victims. It is the source for milestone T063.

title: Security Council resolution 1530 (2004): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (Madrid)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS) Operative text attributes the Madrid bombings to ETA; see NOTES.md.
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1530, adopted on 11 March 2004, the day of the Madrid train bombings. The Council condemns the attacks in the strongest terms, and its operative text attributes them to ETA. That attribution is disputed by a later UN source: milestone T150 records that the UN Special Rapporteur's 2008 report on Spain describes the bombings as carried out by members of an international terrorist cell. CTA6 records what each source says without deciding between them.

title: Security Council resolution 1535 (2004): Establishment of the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1535, adopted on 26 March 2004. It revitalized the Counter-Terrorism Committee created by resolution 1373 and set up the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED), headed by an Executive Director, with the Committee continuing to report to the Council. It is the source for milestone T073; CTED's mandate was later renewed by resolution 2617 (T131).

title: Security Council resolution 1540 (2004): Non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction to non-State actors
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1540, adopted on 28 April 2004 under Chapter VII of the UN Charter, on non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction to non-State actors. It decides that all States shall refrain from supporting non-State actors that attempt to develop, acquire, possess, transfer or use nuclear, chemical or biological weapons and their means of delivery. It is the source for milestone T074.

title: Security Council resolution 1566 (2004): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1566, adopted on 8 October 2004. It condemns all acts of terrorism irrespective of motivation, recalls that criminal acts committed with intent to cause death or serious injury or to take hostages, for the purpose of provoking terror, intimidating a population or compelling a government, are not justifiable, and sets up a working group on measures against individuals and groups. Its wording is one of the two definitions compared in the people-disagree milestone T079, alongside the 1937 League of Nations convention.

title: Security Council resolution 1595 (2005): The situation in the Middle East (International Independent Investigation Commission, Lebanon)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1595, adopted on 7 April 2005, on the situation in the Middle East. At Lebanon's request, it established an international independent investigation commission based in Lebanon to help the Lebanese authorities investigate 'this terrorist act', including identifying its perpetrators, sponsors, organizers and accomplices. The resolution identifies the act as 'the 14 February 2005 terrorist bombing in Beirut, Lebanon, that killed former Lebanese Prime Minister Rafiq Hariri and others'; resolution 1757 later established the Special Tribunal for Lebanon (T095).

title: Security Council resolution 1611 (2005): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (London)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1611, adopted on 7 July 2005, the day of the London transport bombings. The Council condemns the attacks in London without reservation and regards any act of terrorism as a threat to peace and security. It is cited for milestone T086.

title: Security Council resolution 1624 (2005): Threats to international peace and security (incitement to commit terrorist acts)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1624, adopted on 14 September 2005, on incitement to commit terrorist acts. It calls on all States to prohibit incitement by law, in line with their obligations under international law, to strengthen border security, and to promote dialogue among civilizations. It is the source for milestone T087.

title: Security Council resolution 1757 (2007): The situation in the Middle East (Special Tribunal for Lebanon)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1757, adopted on 30 May 2007. Acting under Chapter VII of the UN Charter, the Council decided that the provisions of the annexed document on establishing a Special Tribunal for Lebanon would enter into force. It is the source for milestone T095 and follows the investigation commission set up by resolution 1595 (2005).

title: Security Council resolution 1904 (2009): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (Office of the Ombudsperson)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1904, adopted on 17 December 2009, on the Al-Qaida and Taliban sanctions measures first imposed under resolutions 1267, 1333 and 1390. It continued those measures and created the Office of the Ombudsperson to handle requests from those seeking removal from the sanctions list (milestone T101). It is part of how the Council responded to concerns about the listing process, which also appear in court challenges such as T097.

title: Security Council resolution 1989 (2011): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (Al-Qaida sanctions)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 1989, adopted on 17 June 2011, on the Al-Qaida sanctions measures. Together with resolution 1988 it separated the Taliban and Al-Qaida sanctions regimes, which had been run together since resolution 1267 (milestone T104). It continues the asset-freeze, travel and arms measures from earlier resolutions.

title: Security Council resolution 2170 (2014): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (ISIL and ANF)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 2170, adopted on 15 August 2014, concerning ISIL and the Al-Nusrah Front (ANF). The Council strongly condemns their killing and targeting of civilians and other atrocities, condemns their recruitment of foreign terrorist fighters, and reaffirms that States must prevent arms and other support from reaching them. It is the source for milestone T111; the foreign-fighter resolution 2178 followed a month later (T112).

title: Security Council resolution 2178 (2014): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (foreign terrorist fighters)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 2178, adopted on 24 September 2014, on foreign terrorist fighters. It decides that Member States shall, consistent with international human rights, refugee and humanitarian law, prevent and suppress the recruiting, organizing, transporting or equipping of foreign terrorist fighters, and reaffirms that States must control borders and travel documents. It is the source for milestone T112; resolution 2396 (2017) built on it.

title: Security Council resolution 2253 (2015): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 2253, adopted on 17 December 2015. It renamed the 1267/1989 Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee the '1267/1989/2253 ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee' and extended listing criteria to those associated with ISIL. It is the source for milestone T116 and shows the 1999 sanctions regime being adapted to ISIL.

title: Security Council resolution 2341 (2017): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (critical infrastructure)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 2341, adopted on 13 February 2017, on protecting critical infrastructure against terrorist attacks. It encourages all States to raise awareness of the risks and improve preparedness, and calls on Member States to develop or improve strategies for reducing risks to critical infrastructure. No timeline milestone in CTA6 cites it yet.

title: Security Council resolution 2396 (2017): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (returning and relocating foreign terrorist fighters)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 2396, adopted on 21 December 2017, on returning and relocating foreign terrorist fighters. Building on resolution 2178, it decides that Member States shall use advance passenger information, develop the capability to collect and analyse passenger name record data, and develop watch lists or databases of known and suspected terrorists. It is the source for milestone T124.

title: Security Council resolution 2462 (2019): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (financing of terrorism)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 2462, adopted on 28 March 2019, on countering the financing of terrorism. It reaffirms the financing obligations in resolution 1373 (2001), requires States to criminalize terrorist financing consistent with international humanitarian, human rights and refugee law, and calls for more traceable and transparent financial transactions. It is the source for milestone T126.

title: Security Council resolution 2617 (2021): Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts (CTED mandate renewal)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN Security Council resolution 2617, adopted on 30 December 2021. It decided that the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED) would continue as a special political mission under the Committee's guidance until 31 December 2025, with an interim review by 31 December 2023. It is the source for milestone T131 and continues the body created by resolution 1535 (T073).

title: General Assembly resolution A/RES/3034(XXVII): Measures to prevent international terrorism
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN General Assembly resolution 3034 (XXVII), adopted on 18 December 1972, on measures to prevent international terrorism. It established a 35-member Ad Hoc Committee on International Terrorism appointed by the President of the General Assembly. It is the source for milestone T011 and is the earliest General Assembly resolution on terrorism in CTA6.

title: General Assembly resolution A/RES/40/61: Measures to prevent international terrorism
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN General Assembly resolution 40/61, adopted on 9 December 1985, on measures to prevent international terrorism. It calls on all States to refrain from organizing, instigating, assisting or participating in terrorist acts in other States, or acquiescing in such activities on their territory, and to implement the recommendations of the Ad Hoc Committee on International Terrorism. It is the source for milestone T020.

title: General Assembly resolution A/RES/49/60: Measures to eliminate international terrorism (Declaration)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN General Assembly resolution 49/60, adopted on 9 December 1994, which contains the Declaration on Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism. In the Declaration, UN Member States reaffirm their unequivocal condemnation of all acts, methods and practices of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable, wherever and by whomever committed. It is the source for milestone T034, and later resolution 51/210 reaffirms it.

title: General Assembly resolution A/RES/51/210: Measures to eliminate international terrorism (Ad Hoc Committee)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN General Assembly resolution 51/210, adopted on 17 December 1996, on measures to eliminate international terrorism. It strongly condemns all acts of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable, calls on States to take further measures consistent with international law and human rights standards, reaffirms the 1994 Declaration, and established an Ad Hoc Committee on international terrorism conventions. It is the source for milestone T039.

title: General Assembly resolution A/RES/60/288: The United Nations Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN General Assembly resolution 60/288, adopted on 8 September 2006, which sets out the United Nations Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy with a plan of action annexed. In it Member States resolve to condemn terrorism in all its forms consistently and strongly, as one of the most serious threats to international peace and security. The UN Office of Counter-Terrorism describes it as adopted by consensus; it is the source for milestone T091, and resolution 71/291 later created an office to help implement it.

title: General Assembly resolution A/RES/71/291: Strengthening the capability of the UN system to assist Member States in implementing the Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy (Office of Counter-Terrorism)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
summary: UN General Assembly resolution 71/291, adopted on 15 June 2017, on strengthening the UN system's capability to help Member States implement the Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy. It decides to establish the Office of Counter-Terrorism, with the competencies and functions set out in a report of the Secretary-General (A/71/858). It is the source for milestone T121.

title: About the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED)
notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].
summary: The 'About' page of the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED), on the website of the Security Council's Counter-Terrorism Committee. The site covers the Committee's mandate, Security Council and General Assembly resolutions, country assessments and visits, and implementation surveys. CTA6 cites it for milestone T055 as the Committee's own description of the body created under resolutions 1373 and 1535. The page is undated [UNKNOWN].

title: Security Council resolutions on counter-terrorism (CTC list)
notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].
summary: A list of Security Council resolutions on counter-terrorism kept by the Council's Counter-Terrorism Committee. It is the Committee's own index of the resolutions that define its work and is a finding aid for the resolutions in CTA6. No milestone cites it directly, and the page is undated [UNKNOWN].

title: United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism (home page)
notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].
summary: The home page of the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT). The page says the Office provides leadership, coordination and capacity-building to support Member States in implementing the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy. CTA6 cites it for milestone T121, the 2017 resolution that created the Office. The page is undated [UNKNOWN].

title: International legal instruments (counter-terrorism)
notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].
summary: A page of the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism summarizing the international legal instruments against terrorism. It says that since 1963 the international community has developed 19 instruments under the United Nations and the IAEA, open to all Member States, and gives a short description of each, for example on aircraft, hostages, nuclear material, maritime navigation, bombings and financing. It is the UN's own overview of the treaty framework that the convention entries in CTA6 belong to. The page is undated [UNKNOWN].

title: Terrorism Prevention Branch
author_or_issuing_body: UN Office on Drugs and Crime
notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].
summary: A page of the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) about its Terrorism Prevention Branch. It records that UNODC has a dedicated unit for terrorism prevention; the page's capture shows mostly site navigation, so the Branch's specific mandate is not recorded in CTA6 [UNKNOWN]. The page is undated [UNKNOWN].

title: Multilateral treaties deposited with the Secretary-General, Chapter XVIII (Penal Matters)
notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].
summary: Chapter XVIII (Penal Matters) of the UN Treaty Collection, which lists the multilateral treaties deposited with the UN Secretary-General, including counter-terrorism conventions. It is the official depositary record for those treaties and is cited for milestones T013, T018, T040, T048 and T083. The page is undated [UNKNOWN].

title: Security Council Committee pursuant to resolutions 1267 (1999), 1989 (2011) and 2253 (2015)
notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].
summary: The page of the Security Council committee established under resolutions 1267 (1999), 1989 (2011) and 2253 (2015), now the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee. The committee oversees the sanctions regime that began with resolution 1267, and the UN sanctions site lists it alongside the Council's other sanctions committees. The page is undated [UNKNOWN].

title: 1540 Committee
notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].
summary: The home page of the 1540 Committee, the Security Council committee established under resolution 1540 (2004) on keeping weapons of mass destruction away from non-State actors. The site holds the related resolutions, committee reports and Council briefings. CTA6 cites it for milestone T074. The page is undated [UNKNOWN].

title: Education for Justice University Module Series: Counter-Terrorism
author_or_issuing_body: UN Office on Drugs and Crime
summary: A university module series on counter-terrorism published in 2018 by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime under its Education for Justice (E4J) initiative. UNODC says the modules are a resource for lecturers, giving foundational knowledge of international, regional and national instruments and approaches and encouraging critical thinking. It is a secondary teaching resource, not a record of a specific event.

title: Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft (Tokyo)
notes: Scanned PDF (no text layer); title/date confirmed by OCR of first pages (raw/CONV-TOKYO1963.ocr.txt).
summary: The Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft, concluded in Tokyo on 14 September 1963. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it applies to acts affecting in-flight safety, lets the aircraft commander restrain a person believed to have committed or to be about to commit such an act, and requires States to take custody of offenders. UNOCT lists it as the first of the international legal instruments against terrorism (from 1963); it is the source for milestone T008. The cited copy is a scanned PDF whose title and date were confirmed by OCR.

title: Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft (The Hague)
notes: Scanned PDF (no text layer); title/date confirmed by OCR of first pages (raw/CONV-HAGUE1970.ocr.txt).
summary: The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft, concluded in The Hague on 16 December 1970. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it makes it an offence to seize or control an aircraft in flight by force or threat, requires 'severe penalties', and requires States holding an offender to extradite or prosecute. It is the source for milestone T009; the cited copy is a scanned PDF whose title and date were confirmed by OCR.

title: Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation (Montreal)
notes: Scanned PDF (no text layer); title/date confirmed by OCR of first pages (raw/CONV-MONTREAL1971.ocr.txt).
summary: The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation, concluded in Montreal on 23 September 1971. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it makes it an offence to commit violence on board an aircraft in flight that endangers it or to place an explosive device on an aircraft, and requires States to extradite or prosecute offenders. A 1988 protocol extended it to attacks at airports. It is the source for milestone T010; the cited copy is a scanned PDF confirmed by OCR.

title: Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Crimes against Internationally Protected Persons, including Diplomatic Agents
author_or_issuing_body: UN General Assembly / UN Treaty Collection
notes: Scanned PDF (no text layer); title/date confirmed by OCR of first pages (raw/CONV-IPP1973.ocr.txt).
summary: The Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Crimes against Internationally Protected Persons, including Diplomatic Agents, adopted on 14 December 1973. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it defines protected persons (such as heads of State, foreign ministers and officials entitled to special protection abroad) and requires States to criminalize murder, kidnapping and other attacks on them or their official premises. It is the source for milestone T013; the cited copy is a scanned PDF confirmed by OCR.

title: International Convention against the Taking of Hostages
author_or_issuing_body: UN General Assembly / UN Treaty Collection
notes: Scanned PDF (no text layer); title/date confirmed by OCR of first pages (raw/CONV-HOSTAGES1979.ocr.txt).
summary: The International Convention against the Taking of Hostages, adopted on 17 December 1979. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it defines hostage-taking as seizing or detaining a person and threatening them in order to compel a third party, such as a State or international organization, to act or refrain from acting. It is the source for milestone T018; the cited copy is a scanned PDF confirmed by OCR.

title: Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material
notes: Scanned PDF (no text layer); title/date confirmed by OCR of first pages (raw/CONV-NUCMAT1980.ocr.txt).
summary: The Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material, opened for signature on 3 March 1980 (IAEA). According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it criminalizes the unlawful possession, use, transfer or theft of nuclear material and threats to use it, and 2005 amendments extended protection to nuclear facilities and material in domestic use, storage and transport. It is the source for milestone T019; the cited copy is a scanned PDF confirmed by OCR.

title: International Convention for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings
author_or_issuing_body: UN General Assembly / UN Treaty Collection
notes: Scanned PDF (no text layer); title/date confirmed by OCR of first pages (raw/CONV-BOMBINGS1997.ocr.txt).
summary: The International Convention for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings, adopted by the UN General Assembly on 15 December 1997. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it creates a regime of universal jurisdiction over the intentional use of explosives or other lethal devices in or against defined public places with intent to kill, seriously injure or cause extensive destruction. It is the source for milestone T040; the cited copy is a scanned PDF confirmed by OCR.

title: International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism
author_or_issuing_body: UN General Assembly / UN Treaty Collection
summary: The International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism, adopted by the UN General Assembly on 9 December 1999. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it requires States to prevent and counteract direct or indirect financing of terrorists, including through groups claiming charitable, social or cultural goals, to hold financiers liable, and to identify, freeze and seize funds. It is the source for milestone T048; Security Council resolutions 1373 and 2462 later added binding financing obligations.

title: International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism
author_or_issuing_body: UN General Assembly / UN Treaty Collection
summary: The International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism, adopted on 13 April 2005. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it covers a broad range of acts and targets, including nuclear power plants and reactors, as well as threats and attempts, requires offenders to be extradited or prosecuted, and provides for making nuclear material safe through the IAEA after a crisis. It is the source for milestone T083.

title: Council Framework Decision 2002/475/JHA of 13 June 2002 on combating terrorism
summary: Council Framework Decision 2002/475/JHA of 13 June 2002 on combating terrorism, adopted by the Council of the European Union. It set common EU rules on terrorist offences and defines a 'terrorist group' as a structured group of more than two persons, established over time and acting in concert to commit terrorist offences. It is the source for milestone T062; Directive (EU) 2017/541 followed it in 2017 (T118).

title: Directive (EU) 2017/541 on combating terrorism
author_or_issuing_body: European Parliament and Council of the EU
summary: Directive (EU) 2017/541 of the European Parliament and the Council on combating terrorism, dated 15 March 2017. The Directive states that it establishes minimum rules on the definition of criminal offences and sanctions for terrorist offences, offences related to a terrorist group and related offences, and that Union-wide harmonised rules are needed because Member States acting alone could not achieve its objectives. It is the source for milestone T118 and follows the 2002 Framework Decision (EU-FD2002).

summary: The UK's Explosive Substances Act 1883, as published on legislation.gov.uk. summary: Ireland's Offences against the State Act, 1939 (No. 13 of 1939), as published in the Irish Statute Book. It is the source for milestone T007.

notes: Undated web page; date [UNKNOWN].

title: Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996 (Pub. L. 104-132)
summary: The US Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996 (Pub. L. 104-132), enacted on 24 April 1996. Its long title says it is an Act to deter terrorism, provide justice for victims and provide for an effective death penalty, and it also contains rules for habeas cases brought by State prisoners under capital sentence. It is the source for milestone T038.

title: Authorization for Use of Military Force (Pub. L. 107-40)
summary: The Authorization for Use of Military Force (Pub. L. 107-40), enacted on 18 September 2001. It authorizes the President to use all necessary and appropriate force against those nations, organizations or persons he determines planned, authorized, committed or aided the 11 September 2001 attacks, or harbored them, to prevent future acts of international terrorism against the United States. It is the source for milestone T053, and its continued application was the subject of a 2015 Congressional Research Service report (CRS-R43983).

title: USA PATRIOT Act (Pub. L. 107-56)
summary: The USA PATRIOT Act (Pub. L. 107-56), enacted on 26 October 2001. Its long title says it is an Act to deter and punish terrorist acts in the United States and around the world and to enhance law enforcement investigatory tools; among other things it amended surveillance law, for example to cover electronic communications. It is the source for milestone T056, and parts of it were later reviewed by the Justice Department Inspector General (T094) and the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board (T109).

title: Homeland Security Act of 2002 (Pub. L. 107-296)
summary: The Homeland Security Act of 2002 (Pub. L. 107-296), enacted on 25 November 2002. Its long title says it is an Act to establish the Department of Homeland Security. It is the source for milestone T065; DHS's own history says the Department combined all or part of 22 federal departments and agencies.

title: Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (Pub. L. 108-458)
summary: The Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (Pub. L. 108-458), enacted on 17 December 2004. Its long title says it is an Act to reform the US intelligence community and the Government's intelligence and intelligence-related activities. It is the source for milestone T081 and followed the 9/11 Commission Report of July 2004 (T077).

title: Military Commissions Act of 2006 (Pub. L. 109-366)
summary: The Military Commissions Act of 2006 (Pub. L. 109-366), enacted on 17 October 2006. Its long title says it authorizes trial by military commission for violations of the law of war, and it establishes procedures for trying alien unlawful enemy combatants. It is the source for milestone T092 and one side of the people-disagree milestone T096, because it restricted habeas corpus before the Supreme Court's 2008 ruling.

title: USA FREEDOM Act of 2015 (Pub. L. 114-23)
summary: The USA FREEDOM Act of 2015 (Pub. L. 114-23), enacted on 2 June 2015. Its long title says it reforms the Federal Government's authorities to require the production of business records, conduct electronic surveillance, use pen registers and trap and trace devices, and gather information for foreign intelligence, counterterrorism and criminal purposes. It is the source for milestone T115 and followed the 2014 oversight board report on the Section 215 records program (T109).

title: Executive Order 13224
summary: US Executive Order 13224 of 23 September 2001 on blocking property of designated persons, as published by the Department of State. The order states its objectives include preventing and suppressing terrorism, denying financing and financial services to terrorists and terrorist organizations, and sharing information. It is the source for milestone T054 and is the basis of US terrorist-financing designations.

It created military commissions for certain non-citizens (milestone T058). The Supreme Court later held that the commission convened under it to try one petitioner lacked power to proceed, which is recorded as the people-disagree milestone T090.

title: Executive Order 13491: Ensuring Lawful Interrogations

It is the source for milestone T098.

As recorded in milestone T075, it concerned whether federal courts had jurisdiction over habeas petitions from detainees at Guantanamo. It is the first of the Guantanamo detention cases in CTA6, followed by T090 and T096; according to the syllabus, the Court held that United States courts have jurisdiction to consider challenges to the legality of the detention of foreign nationals captured abroad in connection with hostilities and incarcerated at Guantanamo Bay.

title: H. v. Rumsfeld, 542 U.S. 507 (2004)

summary: The US Supreme Court decision H. v. Rumsfeld, 542 U.S. 507, decided on 28 June 2004. The syllabus records the plurality's conclusion that, although Congress authorized detention of combatants in the narrow circumstances alleged, due process demands that a US citizen held as an enemy combatant be given a meaningful opportunity to contest the factual basis for that detention before a neutral decisionmaker. It is the source for milestone T076.

title: H. v. Rumsfeld, 548 U.S. 557 (2006)
author_or_issuing_body: Supreme Court of the United States (Library of Congress, U.S. Reports)

The Court held that the military commission convened to try the petitioner lacked power to proceed because its structure and procedures violated both the Uniform Code of Military Justice and the Geneva Conventions. It is one side of the people-disagree milestone T090, opposite the 2001 Military Order that created the commissions; Congress then passed the Military Commissions Act of 2006 (T092).

title: B. v. Bush, 553 U.S. 723 (2008)
author_or_issuing_body: Supreme Court of the United States (Library of Congress, U.S. Reports)
summary: The US Supreme Court decision B. v. Bush, 553 U.S. 723, decided on 12 June 2008. The Court held that Guantanamo detainees have the constitutional privilege of habeas corpus and are not barred from seeking it because they were designated enemy combatants or held at Guantanamo, even though section 7 of the Military Commissions Act of 2006 denied courts jurisdiction. It is one side of the people-disagree milestone T096.

title: Northern Ireland (Emergency Provisions) Act 1973
summary: The UK's Northern Ireland (Emergency Provisions) Act 1973, dated 25 July 1973. Its parts cover the trial and punishment of certain offences, offences against public security and public order, and miscellaneous provisions. It is an emergency law for Northern Ireland and the source for milestone T012.

title: Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1974
summary: The UK's Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1974, dated 29 November 1974. Its parts cover proscribed organisations, exclusion orders, and offences, detention and prosecution. As its title states, it was made as a temporary measure; it is the source for milestone T014 and was later replaced by the 1989 Act (UK-PTA1989).

title: Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1989
summary: The UK's Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1989, dated 15 March 1989. Its parts cover proscribed organisations, exclusion, financial assistance for terrorism, powers of arrest, stop and search and detention, and further provisions for Northern Ireland. It is the source for milestone T027 and continues the temporary-provisions model of the 1974 Act.

title: Terrorism Act 2000
summary: The UK's Terrorism Act 2000, dated 20 July 2000. Its parts cover proscribed organisations, terrorist property, terrorist investigations, terrorist offences, and provisions for Northern Ireland. It is the source for milestone T049.

title: Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001
summary: The UK's Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001, dated 14 December 2001. Its parts cover terrorist property and freezing orders, the security of pathogens and nuclear material, aviation, police powers and retention of communications data, and, in Part 4, the certification, detention and deportation of suspected international terrorists. The Part 4 detention powers are the subject of the people-disagree milestone T080, after the House of Lords held a related provision incompatible with the European Convention on Human Rights.

title: Prevention of Terrorism Act 2005
summary: The UK's Prevention of Terrorism Act 2005, dated 11 March 2005, now shown as repealed. Its sections created control orders, both non-derogating orders supervised by the court and derogating orders made by the court. It followed the House of Lords ruling on Part 4 of the 2001 Act (T080) and is the source for milestone T082; the 2011 TPIM Act later abolished control orders.

title: Terrorism Act 2006
summary: The UK's Terrorism Act 2006, dated 30 March 2006. Part 1 creates offences including encouragement of terrorism, dissemination of terrorist publications (with provisions on internet activity), preparation of terrorist acts and terrorist training. It is the source for milestone T089.

title: Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures Act 2011
summary: The UK's Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures Act 2011, dated 14 December 2011. Its first sections abolish control orders and replace them with terrorism prevention and investigation measures (TPIMs), with conditions for imposing them, a five-year limit on TPIM notices, and court scrutiny. It is the source for milestone T106 and replaced the control-order regime of the 2005 Act.

title: Counter-Terrorism and Security Act 2015
summary: The UK's Counter-Terrorism and Security Act 2015, dated 12 February 2015. Its parts cover temporary restrictions on travel, changes to terrorism prevention and investigation measures, data retention, aviation, shipping and rail security, and a duty concerning the risk of people being drawn into terrorism. It is the source for milestone T114.

It is the source for milestone T132.

title: The Belfast Agreement
summary: The Belfast (Good Friday) Agreement of 10 April 1998, as published by the Northern Ireland Office on GOV.UK. The page says the Agreement covered identity and citizenship and made commitments on decommissioning, security, policing and prisoners. It is the source for milestone T041 and marks a political settlement in Northern Ireland, where several earlier UK emergency and terrorism laws applied.

title: Report of the Official Account of the Bombings in London on 7th July 2005
summary: The 'Report of the Official Account of the Bombings in London on 7th July 2005', published by the UK Home Office on 11 May 2006. It is the government's official account of the 7 July 2005 attacks on London's transport system. It is cited for milestone T086; the GOV.UK page confirms publication by the Home Office on 11 May 2006, but the report's contents are not summarized in CTA6 [UNKNOWN] because the PDF itself was not opened.

summary: 'In the Name of Security: Counterterrorism Laws Worldwide since September 11', a Human Rights Watch report dated 29 June 2012. The report states that more than 140 governments have passed counterterrorism legislation since September 11, 2001, and it argues that some of these laws have been used in ways that violate rights such as due process, free expression and privacy. These are Human Rights Watch's findings; CTA6 lists the report as an NGO critique without drawing its own conclusions.

title: Getting Away with Torture: The Bush Administration and Mistreatment of Detainees
summary: 'Getting Away with Torture: The Bush Administration and Mistreatment of Detainees', a Human Rights Watch report dated 12 July 2011. HRW says it summarizes public information on the role of senior US officials in setting post-9/11 interrogation and detention policies, analyzes it under US and international law, and argues there is a basis for a criminal investigation. These are HRW's own conclusions; CTA6 lists it as an NGO critique.

title: Dangerously Disproportionate: The Ever-Expanding National Security State in Europe (EUR 01/5342/2017)
summary: 'Dangerously Disproportionate: The Ever-Expanding National Security State in Europe' (EUR 01/5342/2017), an Amnesty International report of 17 January 2017. Amnesty says it gives a bird's-eye view of the 'securitization' of Europe across eight themes, including states of emergency, privacy, freedom of expression and movement, deprivation of nationality, and transfers to places where people risk torture. These are Amnesty's own assessments; CTA6 lists it as an NGO critique.

title: Security Council resolution 2359 (2017): Peace and security in Africa (G5 Sahel Joint Force)

It is the source for milestone T122; resolution 2391 later addressed support to the force (T180).

title: Security Council resolution 2349 (2017): Peace and security in Africa (Lake Chad Basin)
notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)

The Council strongly condemns terrorist attacks and abuses by Boko Haram and ISIL in the region, including killings, abductions, sexual violence and forced marriage. It is the source for milestone T044 and continues the sequence that began with resolution 731 (T031).

notes: Verified via the English PDF from documents.un.org (ODS)
